title: WATCHERS OF WHAT IS HAPPENING

publication_scope.included: External evidence, public provider status/RCA material, public censorship measurements, public-safe JANUS methodological prior art, user-reported historical observation with explicit evidence status, hypotheses and falsifiers.

github_reference.interpretation: The decisive JANUS anomaly is before GitHub run-object materialization. It is not a runner-allocation delay and it is not record drift.

findings: On 2026-08-26 from 15:02 to 15:45 UTC Actions jobs failed to start and later experienced delayed starts while backlog was drained.

GitHub attributed the incident to write saturation on a database primary used by the service processing Actions workflow triggers, combined with an upstream issue in GitHub event-processing infrastructure that amplified bursts of already-high load.
Primary failover did not fully recover the system; GitHub used throttling and service restarts, then gradually raised throttles while queues burned down.
GitHub stated that downstream throttles used for protection had been configured about 10 percent too high for the degraded system.

A later Actions/Pull Requests incident on 2026-08-26 reported 20 percent of Actions runs delayed more than five minutes and up to four percent failing to trigger; full recovery was reported beginning 23:58 UTC.

facts.finding: Published TSPU measurement research demonstrates in-path, centrally managed but geographically distributed censorship behavior with fine-grained SNI, IP and QUIC triggers and multiple blocking behaviors.
OONI measurements of the March 2026 Telegram block show anomalies across many Russian networks but not every tested network, including resets and timeouts; effects were heterogeneous by AS/network.
On 2026-08-26 Russian users across several providers reported blocking/problems for encrypted DNS services from Google and Cloudflare, including DoH/DoT.

Beginning approximately the evening of 2026-08-26, a public network experiment reported selective interception of plaintext UDP DNS queries addressed to 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1, with TCP DNS still reaching the intended resolver; low-TTL probing pointed toward the Russian National Domain Name System path. This is a researcher observation reported publicly, not an official Russian attribution statement.

tspu_lane.hypothesis: Selective or staged TSPU policy testing can produce asynchronous, protocol-specific and network-specific partial failures rather than one synchronized nationwide outage.
tspu_lane.why_it_matters: This makes selective/staged filtering a technically grounded comparison lane for the 2026-08-26/27 period.
tspu_lane.direct_fit_to_janus_github_anomaly: LOW_WITHOUT_AN_ADDITIONAL_BRIDGE because JANUS observed a GitHub-internal pre-run-object delay while the eventual GitHub-hosted runner was acquired immediately.

openai_lane.finding: OpenAI reported elevated errors affecting Workspace Agents and ChatGPT Work on web/mobile. The public incident page did not publish a root cause in the material captured for this dossier.

center_of_storm.note: This recovers the Center-of-the-Storm / Traveler identity family. It is not by itself the delayed-send experiment.

strict_timeshift.relevance: JANUS had already formalized the distinction between admission, in-flight work, commit windows, too-late abort and proof of quiescence before the August scheduler investigation.

wave_rider_cohort_drain.relevance: Defines admission open/close, in-flight drain, cancel/admission timestamps and a policy of first measuring the tail and then suppressing only demonstrated waste.

observer_finalization_race.finding: Seven excluded target-3 runs exposed an observer-finalization race in which exact exposure could be emitted before the full per-batch cryptographic observer record was durably finalized.
observer_finalization_race.relevance: This is a concrete JANUS precedent for distinguishing externally visible/emitted state from durable finalization and for inserting a finalization barrier.

causal_send_cancel_protocol.relevant_rule: A future causal anomaly requires event identity/nonces and ordinary latency, buffering, timestamp and software explanations to be excluded; the artifact also contains a preregistered CANCEL SEND consistency stress-test.

reported_sequence: A ChatGPT action/request was arranged for a specific time and involved sending/posting three files.
During the visible delay window the operator issued a cancellation instruction.
The three files/data nevertheless reached the destination or otherwise completed the external send.
The operator interpreted the behavior as a vulnerability/race and requested a controlled follow-up experiment; ChatGPT declined the proposed experiment.
time_traveler_cancel_case.search_result_this_pass: The exact source conversation, three-file identifiers and exact timestamps were not recovered from current GitHub code search, Library search or available personal-context retrieval. They must not be invented.

current_ranked_hypotheses.hypothesis: GitHub internal control-plane overload plus residual schedule registration/materialization weakness explains the JANUS C28 anomaly.
Russian TSPU selective/staged filtering changes were independently occurring in the same broad period and can explain some Russia-specific partial service/network failures.
The July ChatGPT three-file cancellation observation belongs to a generic asynchronous point-of-no-return/cancel race failure class.
One coordinated campaign caused GitHub, OpenAI and Russian anomalies.
